quizzes.title: IELTS Reading — Urban Beekeeping
quizzes.description: One shared passage on the left; answer questions on the right. Timed like a short Academic Reading section.
quizzes.passage_html:
Urban beekeeping has grown rapidly in several European cities over the past two decades. Advocates argue that rooftop hives support pollinators, produce local honey, and educate residents about food systems. City councils in places such as Paris and London have even promoted hive installations on public buildings.

Critics, however, caution that dense colonies in flower-poor districts can strain limited nectar resources and increase competition with wild bees. Some ecologists recommend planting native wildflowers before adding more managed hives. Others note that not all urban honey meets commercial quality standards because of air pollution near busy roads.

Despite the debate, community workshops remain popular. Participants learn hive safety, seasonal feeding, and how to harvest frames without harming the colony. Researchers continue to study whether carefully managed urban apiaries can coexist with wild pollinators when floral diversity is improved.

questions.prompt: What is one argument made by critics of urban beekeeping?

options.text: Hives are too expensive for cities to maintain
Dense colonies may compete with wild bees for flowers
Honey from rooftops is always unsafe to eat
Beekeeping reduces tourism in city centres

questions.prompt: According to advocates, rooftop hives can help people learn about:
Which cities are mentioned as promoting hives on public buildings?
Some ecologists recommend planting __________ before adding more managed hives.
Community workshops teach participants about (select all that apply):
The passage states that all urban honey meets commercial quality standards.

quizzes.title: IELTS Reading — Coastal Piers
quizzes.description: A historical passage about seaside piers. Use the shared reading panel on the left.
quizzes.passage_html:
In the late nineteenth century, many coastal towns built piers as leisure destinations. Steamships brought day-trippers who sought entertainment, fresh air, and sea views. Over time, some piers declined as holiday patterns shifted inland, while others reinvented themselves with theatres, arcades, and festivals.

Victorian engineers often used cast iron and timber to create long walkways that stretched beyond the shoreline. Ticket booths, bandstands, and tea rooms made a visit feel like a special outing. Local newspapers advertised evening concerts and firework displays that drew crowds from nearby cities.

Today, heritage groups campaign to restore surviving piers, arguing that they preserve coastal identity and support tourism. Critics sometimes call restoration expensive, yet towns that invest carefully often see returning visitors and new small businesses along the waterfront.

questions.prompt: Why were many piers originally built?
What caused some piers to decline?

options.text: Too many theatres on each pier

questions.prompt: Victorian engineers often used which materials? (select all that apply)
Heritage groups argue that restoring piers can support __________.
The passage says every pier restoration project is inexpensive.

quizzes.title: IELTS Reading — Sleep Quality
quizzes.description: Academic-style extract on sleep quantity vs quality.
quizzes.passage_html:
Sleep researchers distinguish between sleep quantity and sleep quality. Adults who sleep seven to nine hours may still feel unrested if sleep is fragmented by noise, light, or irregular schedules. Consistent bedtimes and darker bedrooms often improve restorative stages of sleep more than simply staying in bed longer.

Electronic screens are a common culprit. Blue light close to bedtime can delay melatonin release, making it harder to fall asleep. Experts therefore recommend dimming devices an hour before bed, or using night-mode settings when screens are unavoidable.

Caffeine also matters. Because it can remain active in the body for several hours, many specialists advise avoiding coffee after mid-afternoon. Exercise earlier in the day, by contrast, is linked with deeper sleep for many people — though intense workouts late at night may have the opposite effect.

questions.prompt: The passage suggests that sleeping longer always means better rest.
Which factor is mentioned as improving restorative sleep?
Blue light close to bedtime can delay __________ release.
According to the passage, which habits can help sleep? (select all that apply)
Recommended adult sleep length mentioned in the passage is about:

quizzes.title: IELTS Reading — Coral Bleaching
quizzes.description: A short science passage on coral stress and recovery.
quizzes.passage_html:
Coral bleaching occurs when stressed corals expel the algae that give them colour and energy. Rising sea temperatures are a major trigger. Some reefs recover if conditions improve quickly; repeated or prolonged heat can lead to widespread mortality.

Scientists monitor bleaching events with satellite sea-surface temperature data and underwater surveys. Local factors such as pollution and overfishing can make reefs less resilient, even when heat stress is moderate.

Conservation strategies include reducing coastal runoff, protecting herbivorous fish that keep algae in check, and, in some projects, cultivating heat-tolerant coral fragments for restoration. Researchers stress that global action on climate change remains essential if large reef systems are to survive this century.

questions.prompt: What do corals expel during bleaching?
Reefs are more likely to recover when:

options.text: All algae permanently leave the reef

questions.prompt: A major trigger for bleaching mentioned in the passage is rising __________ temperatures.
Which local factors can reduce reef resilience? (select all that apply)
Researchers say global action on climate change is essential for large reef systems.

quizzes.title: IELTS Reading — Vocabulary in Context
quizzes.description: Choose the meaning that best fits how the word is used in an Academic Reading–style sentence.

questions.prompt:
"The committee's decision was provisional, pending the final audit."

Provisional most nearly means:

"Researchers remained sceptical of the early results."

Sceptical most nearly means:

"The policy aimed to mitigate the impact of flooding."

Mitigate most nearly means:

"Her account of the experiment was meticulous."

Meticulous most nearly means:

"The findings were inconclusive."

Inconclusive most nearly means:

options.text: Not decisive / not settling the question

questions.prompt:
"The two theories are compatible."

Compatible most nearly means:

options.text: Able to exist or work together
